item.title: Cool, I want more
item.content:encoded:
This is a neat idea, and I really like this version of the "Foundation" as basically an anti-GoC organization. Feels more like Serpents Hand got an upgrade, especially with that dramatic declaration of SECURING and liberating the realms, citizens and technologies oppressed by the GoC, CONTAINING their operatives so they can stand trial, and PROTECTING the refugees the GoC creates. Ironically, I usually roll my eyes at the GoC as smashy smashy, but if they're the only game in town and seek to liquidate and absorb all other Veil organizations into the Coalition, that's pretty neat, and frankly a lot more realistic than smashy smashy.

That said, I will say it's weird to go with 18 O5 equivalents instead of 13. Some of them don't really even seem to add much. Why is a chef in a resistance movement? Do they really need the spider when Black Queen is already representing the Serpent's Hand? I like the way you get Jude's interactions with the others coming through (I get the impression he might be your favourite character as well), but especially with his animosity to the Critic, why would The Critic be part of it? He doesn't even seem to have a role. I also feel like Prometheus Labs, Anderson Robotics, and Church of the Broken God are all a bit too overlapping, but I feel that way about them even in general. This also uses a ton of jargon that's leaving my head spinning. I don't know if the different Types other than Type Green are existing terminology I should know or not. Here I thought the Foundation was bad. It took me a while to realize "Bellfather" isn't what the group calls themselves because of the way the documents are written. Though I do like that their designations are all wordplay like Reefer, Kenner, Kratt, and Barnum. It may be hard to parse, but it does feel "in character".

This does introduce me to a lot of neat characters that I want to read more about, though.

Mostly the biggest problem is that I want more! It's not really a tale so much as it is a really neat set up for a canon. I want to know what this Protectorate is like. I wanna know how they operate in a world where their funds are going to be coming from whatever the rogue CFO of MC&D can swindle, unless the Circus of the Disquieting is doing donation drives. They're able to take prisoners, and harbor refugees even though Threeports seems to have been occupied by the GoC.

  • And you reading this, should you decide to turn this lofty premise into a canon!

I'm not quite as ambitious as you are, but hopefully someone else is!

item.title: Re: Looking for greenlight on my SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there matthewdgodfrey . Let’s take a look at your concept.

So the pitch started off well, and eerie. I like the concept of a communication station receiving messages from the dead. What I like less are the effects on the people who listen to these broadcasts.

I have a feeling you’re struggling with determining these effects as well. What exactly does “uncanny effects on the listener” mean? You mention the listeners become “obsessed with the sound”, eventually leading to their “suicide”. Why? Is this a compulsion effect (which is generally frowned on these days, unless with good reason) or is it simply because it’s painful hearing from a loved one again?

Its mysterious origins could explain why the audio drives only certain listeners to suicide.

Do you see how vague this statement is? There’s no explanation as to how these broadcasts arrived, or why. As the writer, please give us specific details so that we can review the concept. If you want to make the origins mysterious to the reader, you can still do so later in the actual article.

Last, but not least, you’re missing a narrative. Your Central Narrative portion details how the scip works, and not a story about how it works, which usually involves a central character and his/her discovery/experimentation with the anomaly. Another way to rephrase it: what exactly happens to whom upon encountering your scp?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best!

item.title: Re: Gun-thers Armory
item.content:encoded:
Heyo follow up!

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The store itself is now owned by a parent company (potentially MC&D). The reason there is only 1 gun a week is to cause customers to keep coming back to the store and potentially spend more money than they originally anticipated.

I like the MC&D Addition, though, this element doesn't really seem to be brought up again? at least not in much detail. As a result, the GOI feels like a quick placeholder to explain why the store continuously runs and operates.-what is their motive behind this?

-That said, I'm not too familiar MC&D as whole.

Basically, its just a greedy company. Its behind a glass case because they want people's eyes to be drawn to it an make it look valuable. The gun is made anomalous by unknown means which the foundation will try to investigate. Its only closed for a half hour because the greedy company wants to make a lot of money. As for the minor anomalies, its mostly quality of life stuff for the employee and the building, like a restocking fridge in the break room, and an indestructible firing gallery.

My biggest question/issue is motive behind it, while it is clear they want to maximise profits, there isn't much showing why they are so set on this endeavour in particular. And why they are so set on investing so much into a relatively small business.- for the amount of profit they would make, it seems odd that they are so set on keeping this one place open.

Another issue I have is the weapons 'unknown means'. As it stands, there isn't much showing what came out of this investigation, which makes the narrative unfinished and a bit anti-climatic, as there's no clear answer shown here.

The foundation found the place after investigating a surge in anomalous weapons in the local area. The 1 employee thing is again meant to show the greedy company wanting to make as little spending as they can, but I can change the 1 employee if you feel it would be better. The person no longer thinks the guns are non-anomalous, but the dont talk about their job outside of work because they feel it would be very boring to do so because to them it feels like an accountant talking about how they filed their drawer and such, you understand?

Considering this employee gets only 30mins off per week, I'm skeptical as to how he/she would manage to talk about their job with others in that period of time, if it wasn't planed. Along with this, I have trouble believing he/she is here willingly? why would someone give their life up for a job they don't consider important enough to talk about?

The foundation now actively tries to shut down the building through several means, but they keep getting reverted because of the company's seemingly endless supply of funds. They do eventually shut it down by just demolishing it and relocating the shooting gallery.

This aspect makes me worried, as the endless funds make the "company/GOI" feel far to OP.- It pretty much feels like a quick way to allow the store to do anything with no consequences or setbacks.

Along with this, I don't believe the Foundation would try to continuously re-buy or shut down the building itself, if they know it won't work.

(to me) it seems more plausible for them to buy the town or a large sum of land around the building, and close it off to the public that way.- killing it seems un-characteristically destructive of the Foundation, they would only really attempt to kill something if it was absolutely necessary.

In general, the narrative hasn't really changed to much.- It more or less feels like some explanations were sprinkled in here and there, but there's no direction to the narrative or much of a conflict present.- most of my previous questions and issues with the narrative still stand.

In general I'd recommend looking more into the GOI as whole, it may give some insight into how you could tell the narrative or give some interesting potential directions/hooks.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Re: An Exelent Dentist
item.content:encoded:
A small suggestion.

Lead the reader to believe a Foundation psychologist is running the interview, but, at the end, reveal that the detective is actually in the Dentist's Chair.

You write that other than its reproductive cycle, this SCP is a model citizen. No one would suspect that it views patients as fertilizer. By misleading the reader in this fashion, you show us how deceptive this SCP truly is.

The concept is also unnerving, but keeping the detective at the foundation means that he is safe from harm. Likewise, we as readers also feel safe, unless you turn this false sense of security on its head.

Details:

  • Both psychologists and dentists are referred to as doctors.
  • You could start the conversation with "Are you comfortable" to imply that that the detective is in a psychoanalyst's couch over the dentist's chair.
  • Laughing-gas could easily be mistaken for an amnesiac.

item.title: Re: What makes the Foundation the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
I feel like there's kind of 2 questions here.

In regards to leadership, there is a hierarchy, it's just not interesting enough to mention in many stories. Think about the O5's (and the Ethics Committee, who have similar power) like the board of a corporation or president of a state, and fill in all the boring jobs beneath them. Site Directors are the next down in power, and there are many stories on the wiki that involve the end of the world that show Sites still independently functioning.

For the essence, I agree with Nagiros that research is a core practice. The Foundation believes in the status quo, and the status quo objective way to understand the world is science. Beyond that, if you learn to understand an anomaly, then it is no longer anomalous (even if you don't plan to let the world know.) I picture the Foundation as being very academic, with scientists working on many different SCPs collaborating and publishing and sharing knowledge. See Kate Mctiriss's articles for a little taste of this.

If you want the super broad answer, the core essence is Secure, Contain, Protect. Secure and Contain refer to anomalies, while Protect refers to anomalies (from outside forces), humanity (from anomalies), and normalcy (from even knowledge of anomalies).

I know I'm like 7 years late, but why was there no log about what happens when they place a cured pig into the french oven? Or a dead human in the oven? (Its the foundation, they gotta have a corpse stockpile somewhere.)
The sauna's result from placing a live pig in were interesting and raised questions, so putting a cured pig or dead human in there would give some clue, or at least raise more?
Seems like a pretty blatent oversight, especially since it doesn't require sacrificing a D-class unnecessarally.

Speaking of that, I think this is a good example of how to use D-class on an SCP that doesn't explicitly require human sacrifice; The D-Class were only ordered to do things where the outcome was completely unknown, and testing was aborted when a rogue element was introduced that could have killed or injured them. The D-class here felt like what they are supposed to be; Employees.
Disposable, and lowest rung employees, but Essinsial Employees all the same.

Using the player's muscle mass to repair damage to itself? Makes less sense for a game that depends mainly on hand-eye coordination; I'd have this skip inflict similar neurological damage, worsening vision and motor/manual skills instead of taking a literal pound of flesh.

Description: SCP-5129 is a frog carved out of jade, measuring 10 centimeters in length and dated to be approximately 1000 years old. When in its inactive state, it displays no anomalous characteristics. Once activated by its intended user (SCP-5129-1), it begins to emit harmless levels of █████████ radiation, and air pressure within a 3 meter sphere drops to 27.50 Hg. SCP-5129-1 then telepathically hears a voice1 which is unanimously described as having a deep, booming quality. In every test to date, this voice has only been reported saying: "DO YOU WISH TO EMERGE?" If SCP-5129-1 declines, then SCP-5129 immediately returns to an inactive state.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Zyn
– Zyn

Proper clinical tone for an SCP write-up

I'm personally going to disagree with this—there are several instances of non-clinical phrasing, immediately from the description:

SCP-5129 is a small frog carved out of jade, dated to be approximately one thousand years old. While inactive, it displays no anomalous characteristics. When activated by its intended user (who shall be referred to as SCP-5129-1), it begins to emit harmless levels of █████████ radiation, and air pressure within a ten foot sphere drops to 27.50 Hg.

  • "Small" is a vague measurement and can vary in visualization between individuals. Better to give an objective measurement of the frog so people can immediately know what size it is beyond "small".
  • Numbers greater than 10 (and all measurements with units) should be written as numbers, not words. "Approximately 1000 years".
  • The second sentence can be removed since it's kind of commonsense?
  • The bit in the parentheses is overly long, and can be shortened to "designated SCP-5129-1".
  • Feet are not metric measurements; meters should be used instead.
  • It's not stated where the spherical effect occurs with relation to the object.

The rest of the article has similarly non-clinical writing. Not a huge deal all things considered, but noticeable enough to break immersion for some readers.

Footnotes
1. This voice always speaks in the first or preferred language of SCP-5129-1

item.title: Re: Mommy, Daddy, look! A rainbow!
item.content:encoded:
Heyo followup!

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A corrosive light from a spotlight and a hazardous prism come together to shine eight living colours on a wall, from Red all the way to Pink. When out in the world, the colours seem to grow brighter and brighter until the eyes of living beings around them begin to burst.

Overall, there isn't much of an explanation here. It only feels like more fluff has been added, with little to no reason behind it. As a result, the concept a whole feels disjointed, as there's no link between the elements shown, and the skip(s) don't have any clear purpose.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: Adventurous colours wanting out, the rainbow does what it can to break free. However, they're unable to touch anything and speak little English. They tend to scream at D-Class personnel when seen in front of the thick one-way glass pane they use to see the outer world. Each one differs from another, but they all work together to complete one main goal: destroy the spotlight and prism that binds them to the light. Nobody knows what will happen if it's broken.

This feels closer to additional info on the skips behaviour, as the story doesn't really show a clear arc, conflict or characters. While I don't mind the mystery behind the skips motives, there isn't much of a narrative focus on that aspect (nor is there much focus on the questions the concept raised).

Currently, the narrative seems more focused on showing how the skip behaves in containment, rather than expanding on the concept or building up to a payoff/resolution.

Some narrative questions;
- What is the Foundations end goal? what is the skips end goal/motive? what will the conflict be? how should that make the reader feel? how will the flashlight and prism tie into all of this? who are the characters?

Red or green?

After being interviewed the holder confesses that they’d been questioning the morality of the Foundation for some time but had never thought of doing anything about it.

The containment procedures here do a reasonable job of preparing us for the scip, but damn, maybe at least terminate the personnel before incinerating them.

+ more crit
- more crit

Honestly, after the first paragraph of description, I was expecting to hate this. Note that we never received an answer to the natural question, "what does 'quasi-fungal' mean?" I agree with earlier commentators that this suffers from at least two key problems. One, the scip is questionable as an anomaly; its supernatural characteristics are not identified in the description and are barely alluded to in the log. In fact, to keep the "reveal" in the log intact, the description actually misleads us about what is known about the entity. Two, purely in terms of containment breach risk, this thing is Keter and its current containment procedures are woefully inadequate. It can't conceivably be reliably contained without isolating it from the ocean. Granted, that might mean research into how to isolate and contain the scip is ongoing, but the containment procedures should clarify that.

Let me add a third. The submarine log really didn't work for me. It was easy to lose track of who was doing what, and the characters' behavior was pure archetype; the executive's desire to obtain a sample, using an inadequate vessel, after having confirmed the location of the lost shipment, breaks immersion. "Oh, here's the part where the crew is compelled to do something they themselves identify as irrational by the person paying them, who insists on the vessel doing exactly what is necessary for the narrative to proceed and the monster to awaken / activate / etc."

I simplified the idea from nine sheep and music boxes to one.

However, I decided to keep the music box idea because it symbolizes what the mother wants for the child. It plays a lullaby that hopefully puts the child to sleep. This is the mother's desperate (and ultimately futile) way of comforting the child hoping that he gets better. The reason why the child turned into a sheep is that he grew up next to a farm, and whenever he couldn't sleep, he counted the sheep passing by. The mother knows the child likes sheep and that is why the music box has a sheep centrepiece. The reason the music box exists is that it directly connects the mother to the sheep because it was gifted to her son.

Let me know what you think about this response. I can make any necessary changes to improve the idea.

item.title: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): I'm planning to add, to the usual stuff, a short log of the manhunt, three interviews with the driver and a test log - in that order.

Elevator Pitch: A MK II Supra. The faster it goes, the more universally degrading/degenerative its shell becomes - to the point where it can cut clean through practically anything. As a trade-off, it loses speed proportionally to damage done.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

From the American midwest and moving south, a retired stuntman drives recklessly and attracts the police. In chases, he uses the car to his advantage - cutting through roadblocks and anything else that stands in his way. The Foundation is, of course, not very fond of this, and teams up with the FBI for a manhunt, which lasts 2 whole days and ultimately ends with a cleverly placed spike strip.

The old man is then brought in in a heavily intoxicated state, high on cocaine and MDMA. The three separate interviews are conducted within 1, 3 and 7 days inside his padded holding cell, which reveal the man's motivation to be a combination of forced retirement, an uneventful lifestyle and poverty. The straw that broke the camel's back was the death of his only friend, whose will provided him with the built black-on-yellow car. Realizing his life is already lived and not going to get better, the old man is overcome by rage and sadness. In that moment, he snaps and decides to go out with a bang - by buying copious amounts of drugs and embarking on a journey to the Californian West Coast, where he had once spent the brightest days of his youth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The old man's story and interviews with a side serving of experiments conducted on the car.

Additional Notes: I'm debating, whether or not I should make the car's abilities wane over time as per active use.

The old man's friend knew of the anomalous properties, and kept it locked up in a rented garage out of fear and paranoia.

The car was first found left in the middle of his car lot one night.

item.title: New SCP Concept
item.content:encoded:
I recently came up with my own SCP and I thought I'd give the concept for critique.

This SCP basically looks like an 18-20 year old human male with dark golden-brown hair, green/hazel eyes, and a nanosuit that covers most of his body, apart from his head. It identifies by either the name C-13 or its SCP designation. The nanosuit is made of an unknown material that seems to be living metal with the same DNA as the SCP. The SCP can also directly control the nanosuit, and it can form anything the SCP thinks of, from tools and weapons to vehicles and furniture. The nanosuit can multiply and divide its numbers to create any object of any size, and they can even separate from the suit to exist as separate objects.

The SCP would possibly be classed as Keter, since the SCP can create an object that would allow it to escape containment, though it mostly seems willing to remain in containment. However, the SCP could also be classed as Thaumiel, since it could be utilized to ensure containment for other SCPs.

That's basically my SCP concept. Let me know how it is and how it can be improved.
